_doc: Parity gate contract. ratio = python_time / go_time at reference_scale; r_min is the minimum acceptable ratio. A workload passes when best measured ratio >= r_min AND (where baseline < regression_check_ceiling) has not regressed below baseline by more than tolerance. r_min seeded at 0.65x the measured ratio to absorb Python-side run-to-run variance on a shared machine; the ratio conflates Go time (controlled) with Python time (noisy), so the gate's strongest guarantee is the absolute r_min floor. Re-seed this file and parity_baseline.json from the same run when committing a new top30_summary.json, ideally on a quiescent machine. r_min<1.0 requires justification; out_of_scope excluded. Metadata-only ops (row/clone/rename/drop) use an order-of-magnitude floor instead of the 0.65x rule: their ratio divides two microsecond-scale timings, so run-to-run variance far exceeds 35%, and the floor only has to catch a regression from O(columns) back to O(rows).

DataFrame/drop_nulls.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars now parallelizes the null scan and shards the per-column gather across all cores, but the gather is memory-bandwidth-bound and the string column's Go-pointer storage forces GC write barriers that Polars' byte-layout avoids, so it floors at the measured 1M ratio. Ratchet upward as the path improves.

DataFrame/fill_null.justification: Single-pass typed fill; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.

DataFrame/filter.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars fuses the predicate eval and the multi-column gather into one worker wave (no per-column spawn waves, no []int keep list), but the 20.8 MB output allocation plus GC scanning of []string headers keeps the 1M materialization behind Polars' byte-layout engine. Ratchet upward if the residual allocation/GC cost is ever attacked.

DataFrame/group_by.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars now parallelizes the predicate eval and the per-column gather, but floors at the measured 1M ratio. Ratchet upward as the path improves.

DataFrame/head.justification: Sub-microsecond fixed overhead dominates at this scale; not materialization-bound.

DataFrame/join.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars now parallelizes the predicate eval and the per-column gather, but floors at the measured 1M ratio. Ratchet upward as the path improves.

DataFrame/sort.justification: Already on the parallel-merge radix; the remaining gap is that pairwise merge costs log2(workers) fork-join waves plus O(n) merging, measured at 37.6% pthread_cond wait/signal and 11.5% mergeInto. Capping the range count at the measured optimum recovered part of it. Closing the rest needs an MSD-partition radix (no merge waves) with an adaptive partition byte - deferred, see pkg/chunk/radix.go.

DataFrame/tail.justification: Sub-microsecond fixed overhead dominates at this scale; not materialization-bound.

DataFrame/unique.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars now parallelizes the predicate eval and the per-column gather, but floors at the measured 1M ratio. Ratchet upward as the path improves.

DataFrame/clone.justification: Shares column buffers with the source (Polars clone semantics) instead of deep-copying. Floor catches a regression back to a deep copy (3.02 ms vs 1.6 us at 1M); microsecond-scale ratio, so deliberately not 0.65x of measured.

DataFrame/drop.justification: Retained columns are shared, not copied. Floor catches a regression back to per-column cloning (1.43 ms vs 1.3 us at 1M); microsecond-scale ratio, so deliberately not 0.65x of measured.

DataFrame/rename.justification: Metadata-only: renamed and untouched columns alike share buffers. Floor catches a regression back to per-column cloning (2.07 ms vs 2.3 us at 1M); microsecond-scale ratio, so deliberately not 0.65x of measured.

DataFrame/is_empty.justification: Newly added migration-surface op; O(1) and noise-dominated. Reported but non-gating until a baseline is seeded.

DataFrame/item.justification: Newly added migration-surface op; O(1) and noise-dominated. Reported but non-gating until a baseline is seeded.

DataFrame/row.justification: Reads only the requested row from each column (no whole-frame materialization). Floor catches a regression back to materializing every row, which measured ~94000x slower at 1M; deliberately not 0.65x of measured, because this ratio divides two microsecond-scale timings and its run-to-run variance far exceeds 35%.

DataFrame/vstack.justification: Newly added migration-surface op; not yet calibrated. Reported but non-gating until a baseline is seeded.

DataFrame/iter_rows.justification: Newly added migration-surface op; row-wise materialization is an anti-pattern in both engines. Reported but non-gating until a baseline is seeded.

DataFrame/to_arrow.justification: Newly added migration-surface op; not yet calibrated. Reported but non-gating until a baseline is seeded.

DataFrame/write_csv.justification: Cells are appended into a reused byte buffer (no per-cell string) and row ranges are formatted concurrently, written in row order: 223.6 ms -> ~32 ms at 1M. Still reported non-gating because the timing includes filesystem write-back, so it is not a like-for-like compute comparison across machines.

DataFrame/write_parquet.justification: Non-gating, and deliberately so: a breakdown at 1M puts 86.6% of the time and all 4.6M allocations inside the third-party pqarrow encoder, versus 10.7% in the frame->Arrow conversion gopolars owns (16.3 ms of 151.5 ms). Neither the codec (uncompressed 145.8 ms vs snappy 150.7 ms) nor the row-group size changes that. Reaching parity would mean replacing the parquet encoder, which is a separate proposal.

Expr/fill_nan.justification: Single-pass typed fill; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.

Expr/fill_null.justification: Single-pass typed fill; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.

Expr/over.justification: Partition ids are now built across all cores (the sharded group builder), which is where a profile put ~85% of this op; the per-partition scan stays sequential single-pass because it measured at only ~15% of the cost. gopolars is now ahead of Polars here.

Expr/rank.justification: Uses the parallel-merge radix argsort (it previously called the sequential one), with the range count capped at the measured optimum. Essentially at parity now.

Expr/rolling_max.justification: Floor tracks the measured 1M ratio; ratchet upward as the path improves.

Expr/rolling_min.justification: Floor tracks the measured 1M ratio; ratchet upward as the path improves.

Series/drop_nans.justification: Polars runs this op multi-threaded over chunked Arrow; gopolars now parallelizes the predicate eval and the per-column gather, but floors at the measured 1M ratio. Ratchet upward as the path improves.

Series/fill_nan.justification: Single-pass typed fill; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.

Series/is_not_null.justification: Boolean validity mask produced single-pass; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.

Series/is_null.justification: Boolean validity mask produced single-pass; floor tracks the measured 1M ratio.
